title: Tight Storming Retry Loop
pattern: A loop that repeatedly invokes a failing network/IO dependency immediately after a failure without backoff delays.
why_bad: If an external dependency is failing or overloaded, immediate retries act as a distributed denial-of-service attack from your own clients [39:50]. This amplifies server load, prevents recovery, and triggers a cascading meltdown of the downstream service [13:107].
detection: A loop surrounding a network or database call that checks for errors and retries without invoking an adaptive or static wait mechanism between attempts [13:107].
fix: Introduce exponential backoff with random jitter on all retry mechanisms to decouple client request bursts [39:51].
source: *Database Internals* (Petrov), Part II: Distributed Systems; *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* (Adkins), Chapter 12 [39:50, 13:107].
